Subject: Clarify audit window boundary for Acme (SOC 2 Type II)

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question as we prepare Acme's testing matrix: your current SOC 2 Type II report lists the period ending 2024-12-31 and notes a point-in-time snapshot for "EOD" evidence. Acme's environment had a data retention policy change effective 2025-03-15 and a migration on 2025-03-28. For our procedures we need to confirm exactly what you consider the end boundary for a "month" in delivered evidence (UTC vs local), and whether you provide explicit point-in-time extracts for transitions that occur mid-month.

Specific asks:
- Do your delivered evidence extracts represent calendar-month inclusivity (i.e., include activity up to 23:59:59 UTC on the last day of the month)?
- For a service cutover that happens mid-month, do you provide an EOD snapshot for the prior and post cutover states and a bridge letter explaining any gaps?
- If you do partial-month coverage with point-in-time files, what timestamp format and timezone are used in the CSV logs (ISO 8601 preferred)?

We'd like to document this in the Acme report and, if needed, request a bridge letter to cover the 2025-03 partial month. Can you confirm? If you have a short procedural note you can attach, that would speed things up.

Thanks,
Evan Gray
Senior Engagement Manager
Brightline Audit

Subject: Re: Clarify audit window boundary for Acme (SOC 2 Type II)

Evan —

Thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front: yes, we use calendar-month inclusivity based on UTC and we provide point-in-time EOD extracts for both sides of a mid-month migration plus a short bridge letter when the change affects retention or logging schemas. More details below and I attached example files.

Details / Evidence protocol:
- Month boundary: all standard monthly extracts are inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC on the last day. That is our default for delivered CSV logs and the reporting in the Type II report.
- Mid-month transitions: when a cutover/migration is known, we generate two EOD snapshots (pre-cutover and post-cutover) with timestamped filenames, and a brief bridge letter that explains why there is split coverage and confirms there were no changes to control objectives impacted by the migration.
- Timestamp format: all delivered logs use ISO 8601 with explicit timezone (e.g., 2025-03-31T23:59:59Z). We also include a manifest that maps internal event IDs to exported rows.

What I'm attaching now: 1) redwood-soc2-typeii-202403-report.pdf (report reference), 2) evidence-log-2025-03-31.csv (example EOD extract with ISO timestamps), 3) bridge-letter-template-2025-04.docx (internal template we use to draft client letters).

Proposed next steps:
1) Brightline — confirm whether you want us to generate both the 2025-03-14 EOD (pre-cutover) and 2025-03-28 EOD (post-cutover) extracts as separate CSVs.
2) If yes, we'll produce the extracts and a short bridge letter draft for your review. We can redact any sensitive identifiers if needed.

Cc'ing Karthik (Compliance) and Marissa (GTM/Customer) to coordinate delivery and any messaging to Acme.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
